checks.description: Frontmatter has exactly name and description, name matches the directory.
checks.rule: YAML frontmatter contains keys name and description only; name equals 'email-copy'.

checks.description: Each email variant has id, segment, headline, body, one cta, language.
checks.rule: Every variant object includes id, segment, headline, body, cta, language (ar|en).

checks.description: Each email carries exactly one clear CTA.
checks.rule: Each variant has a single cta; no email lists two competing actions or buttons.

checks.description: Body is short, two to four short lines for a busy reader.
checks.rule: Body stays within roughly two to four short lines; no long paragraphs.

checks.description: No em dash character anywhere in the file or example copy.
checks.rule: The file contains zero U+2014 em dash characters.
No Eastern Arabic numerals (U+0660 to U+0669); digits are 0-9 only.

checks.description: No tatweel or kashida in Arabic copy.
checks.rule: The file contains zero U+0640 tatweel characters.

checks.description: No invented offer, price, Skill Path title, or instructor name.
checks.rule: Body references only offers and prices traceable to the brief; absent ones trigger stop-and-ask.
The email speaks to what the reader can build, not to what they lack; no shaming.

checks.description: Named copy frameworks stay optional, the Arabic-first voice stays primary.
checks.rule: The 4 Us, PAS, AIDA, and the 4 Cs are offered as optional tools to test a line against and matched to funnel stage; they are not imposed as mandatory structure over the voice.

checks.description: The paired subject set carries a deliberate preheader.
checks.rule: The subject_lines set paired by subject_ref carries a deliberate preheader (roughly 40 to 90 characters, true to the body), set on purpose rather than spilled body text.

checks.description: The subject is 20 to 60 characters, mobile band roughly 30 to 40, key word in the first 30.
checks.rule: The primary subject runs 20 to 60 characters, sits in the mobile band of roughly 30 to 40, and front-loads the key word inside the first 30 characters so the angle lands before truncation.

checks.description: A deliberate preheader of about 40 to 90 characters that adds a promise, not a repeat of the subject.
checks.rule: The preheader is set on purpose, runs about 40 to 90 characters, adds a promise rather than repeating the subject, and is never left to spill body text.

checks.description: The email states its send trigger: time-based or behavior-triggered.
checks.rule: The email states a send_trigger as time-based (a delay after the entry event) or behavior-triggered (a response to what the contact did or did not do), layered on the time-based foundation.

checks.description: The single CTA and angle serve the objective of the sequence the email belongs to, for its audience.
checks.rule: The email names its sequence pattern and objective from sequence-standards.md, and its one CTA and angle serve that objective for that audience (relationship, activation, attendance, conversion, reactivation, or win back), measured by the objective metric, not opens.
